Answer: D
Reason: The CT images demonstrate numerous thin-walled cysts diffusely distributed throughout both lungs with no zonal predominance or sparing, which is the hallmark radiographic finding for lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) in a young female. This pattern distinguishes it from Langerhans cell histiocytosis (which typically spares the costophrenic angles and affects upper/mid zones) and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (characterized by reticulation and honeycombing rather than diffuse cysts).
